checkpoints.description: [6/6] Final hardening and release: edge-case tests (an empty world and a dead world keep ticking; a shocked world still round-trips through a save exactly), a 10k-tick soak on the default world (determinism, bounded fossil memory, throughput), an MIT LICENSE, a 1.0.0 version with a --version flag, and the release notes; then the publish cockpit to close the task.

[6/6] Hardening and 1.0.0 release complete: resilience tests (empty world and dead world keep ticking; a shocked world round-trips through a save exactly), exact extinction-episode semantics documented, 10k-tick soak verified (812 ticks/s, deterministic across a save/reload at tick 5000, 183 creatures over 69 species, 173 events inside the bounded log), MIT LICENSE, version 1.0.0 with a --version flag (help in 111 ms), 83/83 tests in about 1.7s; checklists: passed.
Task 'task-primordia-core-v1' completed successfully.

[1/5] Audit and 1.0.1 patch: (1) validate WorldConfig invariants and route bad configs through a friendly CLI error; (2) persistence hardening - version mismatches become readable SaveErrors instead of quarantine, a missing primary with a live backup restores itself, failed replaces leave no temp file; (3) meteor and bloom become true Euclidean discs as documented; (4) web and CLI polish - no-store caching, quiet favicon, capped POST bodies, observatory sessions persist operator changes back to their save on exit, REPL row-count edges; (5) docs, ADR-007, version 1.0.1, full verification and release.

impact_assessment.why: A post-release audit found contract mismatches and durability edges: shock geometry contradicts its documentation, a newer save version is destroyed as corrupt, invalid world configs crash deep in the tick loop, and observatory sessions lose their work.
impact_assessment.benefits: Honest geometry; user saves never quarantined by version drift; recoverable crash windows; no lost sessions; clearer CLI failures.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: shock geometry and web exit persistence change observable behaviour; dependency: none; concurrency: the observatory lock model is unchanged; state: validation must not break existing saves or determinism.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for every behaviour change; full suite plus a determinism replay after each milestone; docs and ADR updated with the code.

checkpoints.description: [1/5] WorldConfig now validates its shape, pace, food, water and season ranges at construction (positive width and height, day_length at least 1, positive food_cap, non-negative food_regrowth and temperature_swing, initial_food_share, water_ratio and season_amplitude within [0, 1]) and the CLI turns the resulting ValueError into a friendly exit 2 with a Fix line; 3 new tests plus 10 sub-cases; checklists: passed.

[2/5] Persistence hardened: a save version this build cannot read raises a readable SaveError with Why and Fix and is never quarantined (previously the file was moved aside as corrupt); a missing primary with a live .bak restores itself on load; a failed replace removes its temp file instead of leaving .tmp_ leftovers; 3 new tests; checklists: passed.

[3/5] Meteor and bloom now sweep a true Euclidean disc (squared distance at most squared radius, boundary inclusive) as their docstrings and the README always promised, instead of a Chebyshev square, for both the tiles they take and the creatures they kill; 1 new geometry test; checklists: passed.

[4/5] Web and CLI polish: the observatory answers Cache-Control no-store on every response, serves /favicon.ico as 204 instead of a 404 body, and caps POST bodies at 4 KiB so an oversized form is refused with the 400 page; the web command saves operator-driven session changes (steps, shocks) back to its save file on exit only when snapshot_hash moved, so untouched saves stay untouched; the REPL now refuses a zero-row species or fossil count instead of quietly showing ten; 5 new tests; checklists: passed.

[5/5] Release 1.0.1: README reflects the audit (status v1.0.1, save-version refusal and crash-window recovery, observatory session persistence, 95-test tally), ADR-007 records every decision, version bumped in __init__ and pyproject, verified --version 1.0.1, same-seed hash equality and an exact save/load replay over 400 ticks; checklists: passed.
Task 'task-primordia-audit-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Second hardening pass over the 1.0.1 review: (1) persistence edges - reading a folder or unreadable file becomes a SaveError with Why and Fix instead of a bare OSError, saving onto an existing folder is refused instead of renaming the folder away, a JSON without a version field gets an honest not-a-primordia-save message, and a quarantine that cannot move the file becomes a SaveError; (2) web and CLI edges - a malformed or negative Content-Length is refused with the 400 page instead of a handler crash or a read-until-EOF hang, an out-of-range port or failed bind becomes a SaveError asking for another port, the web pre-roll persists on exit like the rest of the session while a bare view stays read-only, and binding beyond loopback prints a no-authentication warning; (3) docs, ADR-008, version 1.0.2 and the release.

impact_assessment.why: Reviewing the 1.0.1 changes found failure paths that still traceback or destroy state: save_to onto a folder renames the folder away, stats on a folder raises a raw OSError, a negative Content-Length deadlocks a request thread, web --ticks silently discards its pre-roll, and an unauthenticated socket exposed beyond loopback warns nobody.
impact_assessment.benefits: The Why and Fix promise now holds on the filesystem and socket edges too; no destructive surprises; a hung request is impossible; requested work survives the session; operators are warned before exposing a mutating server.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: web --ticks persists on exit and saving onto a folder is refused; dependency: none; concurrency: the lock model is unchanged, only stricter body parsing; state: the engine, saves written so far and determinism are untouched.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for every behaviour change; full gates at each milestone; small milestoned commits with explicit staging.

checkpoints.description: [1/3] Persistence edges hardened: reading a folder (or an unreadable file) raises a SaveError with Why and Fix instead of a bare OSError; saving onto an existing folder is refused before anything moves; JSON without a version field reports 'not a primordia save' without quarantine; a quarantine whose move fails raises a SaveError and leaves the file in place. 4 new failing-first tests; 99/99 tests in 1.9s; checklists: passed.

[2/3] Web and CLI edges hardened: POST bodies declare a non-negative Content-Length within the 4 KiB cap or get the 400 Why/Fix page (no crash, no read-to-EOF hang); an out-of-range port or refused bind raises a SaveError that asks for another port; the web pre-roll is included in the session hash so --ticks changes persist on exit while a bare view leaves the save untouched; a bind beyond loopback prints a no-authentication warning. 7 new failing-first tests; 106/106 tests in 2.5s; 4/4 gates; checklists: passed.

[3/3] Release 1.0.2: README documents the filesystem refusals, request-body validation, bind errors, loopback warning and pre-roll persistence with the 106-test tally; ADR-008 records every decision; version bumped in __init__ and pyproject; verified primordia 1.0.2, an exact save/load replay through 300+200 ticks, 106/106 tests and 4/4 gates; checklists: passed.
Task 'task-primordia-fixes-v2' completed successfully.

[1/4] Third hardening pass from a full-code audit: (1) simulation correctness - maintain the spatial hash through movement, death and birth instead of querying stale start-of-tick positions; stop a second stride from overshooting its target; make the ancestral template the species-1 founder so every jittered founder is provably within the speciation distance (17 of 300 seeds currently start with two species); (2) input and snapshot integrity - WorldConfig rejects non-integer shapes, non-finite numbers and wrong types, Engine.spawn rejects non-finite energy, save loading validates layer lengths, creature bounds and species references (currently a short terrain/food layer or an out-of-bounds creature loads and later crashes with IndexError), and dump refuses NaN; (3) honest determinism and statistics - snapshot_hash covers the RNG, temperature, registry and fossil instead of only creatures and food, and analytics count living creatures only; (4) README, ADR-009, version 1.0.3 and the release.

impact_assessment.why: The audit found real defects beyond the documented contract: the neighbour hash is stale for the whole tick after any move, founders sometimes split into two species at tick 0, hostile or truncated saves load and then crash deep in the tick loop, and the determinism hash cannot see RNG divergence.
impact_assessment.benefits: Interactions use actual positions; founders honor the one-ancestral-species promise; malformed saves are quarantined with Why/Fix instead of crashing later; nondeterminism in the RNG is detectable; population statistics match their docstrings.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: neighbour selection, founder classification and snapshot_hash values change; dependency: none; concurrency: none (single-threaded engine); state: the save schema is unchanged but a previously loadable malformed snapshot may now be refused; performance: bucket updates add O(tile occupancy) work per move and the richer hash is only computed on demand.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for each behaviour; full gates and a fixed-seed determinism replay after each milestone; small milestones with explicit staging.

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Simulation correctness: the neighbour hash is now updated on every move, death and birth so interactions use actual positions (previously a creature was queried at its start-of-tick tile all tick); newborns killed in their birth tick are not retained; the second stride stops on its target instead of overshooting; the ancestral template itself founds species 1, so every jittered founder is at most 0.15 RMS from it and the herd is provably one species. 5 new failing-first tests (including 120 seeds); 111/111 tests in 2.1s; 3000-tick soak at 887 ticks/s with 151 creatures and 47 species; checklists: passed.

[2/4] Input and snapshot integrity: WorldConfig now requires integer width/height/day_length and finite numeric fields, so NaN, infinity, strings and 1.5-tile worlds fail at construction instead of deep in world/engine code; Engine.spawn refuses non-finite/negative energy and non-integer coordinates; save loading verifies layer lengths, terrain/food/temperature/phase ranges, unique cids, in-bounds land positions, species references, sequential registry ids, ancestors, birth ticks, fossil traces/events and capacity; dump_text refuses NaN (save_to turns it into a SaveError) and a directory .bak is treated as unusable. 12 new tests; 123/123 in 2.5s; long-run save/load hash equal with 19 species and 29 events; 4/4 gates; checklists: passed.

[3/4] Honest determinism and statistics: snapshot_hash now covers the seed, config, raw RNG state, terrain, season phases, food, temperature, every species record, the registry distance and the full fossil record, so an RNG-only or climate-only divergence is visible (about 1 ms per call, on demand only); species_counts and trait_means ignore dead creatures as their docstrings already promised. 2 new tests (four mutation probes plus a dead-population check); 125/125 in 2.4s; same-seed full-state hash and save/load replay still exact; 4/4 gates; checklists: passed.

[4/4] Release 1.0.3: README documents live neighbour bookkeeping, the guaranteed single founder species, full-state determinism hashing, treated snapshots and the 125-test tally; ADR-009 records the audit, decisions, costs and consequences; version bumped in __init__ and pyproject; verified primordia 1.0.3, friendly exit 2 on an invalid world, exact save/load replay through tick 500, 125/125 tests and 4/4 gates; checklists: passed.
